title: Will the highest daily number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz as reported by the IMF PortWatch be at least 10 in Oct 2026?
rules: If the highest daily number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz as reported by the IMF PortWatch is at least 10 in Oct 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

blind.reasoning: Every October PortWatch figure I found is 4 or lower, and traffic has collapsed further since mid-October under an Iranian mine and attack campaign with no deal in sight. The main route to YES is an unseen day around October 5–9, when an independent AIS tracker counted 10–17 crossings a day. PortWatch usually counts only 40–80% of that tracker's figure, so one of those days could still reach 10. A late-October reopening or data revisions are smaller paths.
blind.falsifier: PortWatch data showing a day of 10 or more transits in October (e.g., Oct 5 or Oct 7), or a sudden US-Iran deal that brings an escorted surge of AIS-visible ships before Oct 31.

final.reasoning: The low market price implies the published PortWatch data through Oct 18 has no day of 10 or more, removing my main route to YES (the unseen Oct 5–17 days). What remains is a late-October recovery during a mine blockade with a 0.9/day recent average, or a data revision. Both look less likely than 18.5%.
